change: Leaving ANALOG BD in the active Part also writes the stock FLEX defaults into the engine's copy of the track (0x80000810 + 72 x track, +0 and +0x20).
A new ANALOG BD assignment in the active Part also writes the drum's defaults there.

Leaving ANALOG BD in the active Part clears the track's stock voice flag (0x800049d8 + 168 x track): stock's sample fetch at 0x40007960 writes silence while it is 0, and the trig start at 0x4000f450 sets it again.
why: ANALOG BD is FLEX to stock. A change between the two is no machine change, so stock keeps the engine's copy of the track; and every trig on an ANALOG BD track starts stock's FLEX voice from the drum's bytes read as FLEX settings, which the track then plays after the change until its next trig.
verifyOn015Source: the engine-copy cases fail at the first one, as expected
